suspend the Question Hour to take up a Motion under Rule 168 of the Rules of

Commission Report and Action Taken thereon by the Government.

Road link to Myanmar 
*261. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Wi ll the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are contemplating to take initiative in extending road-links 
to Myanmar across the North-Eastern States according to the 'look east' policy; 
(b) if so, the response received from other countries; and 
(c) if not, whether any other similar programme is being contemplated? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) to (c) Government of India is undertaking a variety 
of cross-border projects with a view to improving connectivity 
 
1

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
between the North-Eastern States of India and Myanmar. Expansion of road 
links between the two countries constitutes an important aspect of these 
initiatives. 
In 2001, Government of India upgraded the 160 km. long Tamu-Kalewa-
Kalemyo in Myanmar which links India and Myanmar through the Tamu-Moreh 
(Manipur) border point. The Tamu-Kalewa-Kalemyo road was used during the 
first India-ASEAN car rally flagged off by the Prime Minister from Gawahati 
in November 2004. In addition, Government of India is committed to 
improving road connectivity at Zowkhathar (Mizoram)-Rhi, the second border 
trade point along the India-Myanmar border, by upgrading the Rhi-Tidm and Rhi-
Falam roads in Myanmar. 
Discussions are also underway for building a Trilateral Highway from 
Moreh in Manipur to Mae Sot in Thailand via Bagan in Myanmar. This 
would provide connectivity to North-East India up to Thailand and beyond to 
other ASEAN countries. 
Further, the Kaladan Multi-modal transport project which is expected to be 
implemented soon seeks to connect Indi an ports on the eastern coast with 
Mizoram through a combination of sea, inland waterway and highway 
connections. The highway component of the project would connect Kaletwa in 
Myanmar with the National Highway 54 at Nalkawn in Mizoram. 
The Myanmar Government has been cooperating with India on the above road 
projects. Thailand, which is involved in the Trilateral Highway project, is also 
keen to implement it.

Impact of tsunami 
*264. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY:  Will the Minister of OCEAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any scientific analysis has been carried out for ascertaining the 
impact and havoc brought by the recent tsunami in the country; 
(b) if so, the details in this regard; 
(c) the measures that are contemplated to forecast tsunami and such other 
disasters in future and to meet the cha llenges thrown by such disasters in the 
future; 
(d) whether experts have suggested creating mangroves on the shores to 
minimize the impact of tsunami; and 
(e) if so, the details in this regard and Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) and (b) Yes Sir. A total of 2260 
line km. of coastal length was impacted by the 26th December, 2004 tsunami 
which included the entire coast of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of 
Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala & Pondicherry. An estimated 12407 
human lives were lost. Estimated loss in monetary terms including damage to 
property amounts to Rs. 11544 Crores. 
Preliminary scientific assessment of the impact of tsunami has been 
conducted by various institutions and Government Departments on 
infrastructure and environment in the coastal areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 
parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra  Pradesh. The Department of Ocean 
Development's vessels ORV Sagar Ka nya and FORV Sagar Sampada were 
deployed for studying the impact of tsunami on ocean environment and its 
resources in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea during January—February 2005. 
The multi disciplinary and multi parameter data collection was so planned as to 
cover areas for which pre-tsunami data was available and also to collect new 
data in new areas. 
6 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
The tsunami waves have caused changes in the biological community of the 
coastal areas by transporting biological organisms from one area to other area 
along the same coast. These changes are likely to be short-term. The coral 
reefs of South Andaman Islands have been found to be damaged and covered 
with debris, mud and sand. There has been no significant impact on demersal 
fisheries. Coastal water quality investigations have indicated enrichment of 
nutrients and contamination by bacteria in the near shore waters of Tamil 
Nadu. Reverse trend was observed for water quality along Kerala Coast. 
(c) It has been proposed to set up a Tsunami and Storm Surge Early 
Warning system with the following components: 
• Strengthening of the existing seismological network to indicate in near 
real time occurrence of tsunamigenic earthquakes. 
• Installation of tsunami warning sensors close to the ocean bottom at 
appropriate locales in the Indian Ocean, with real time connectivity. 
• Tide gauge and data buoys networking to validate arrival of tsunami waves 
at the coast. 
• Modelling of the inundation scenarios for the entire coast and 
mapping of potential risk areas. 
• The establishment of a centre for collection of information, analysis and 
generating status advisories. 
The warning system is scheduled to be operational by September 2007. 
The system will require 10-12 Bottom Pressure Recorders (BPR) close to the 
ocean bottom w ith complementary floating data buoys with real time 
connectivity. Tide gauge networking has already been initiated and six of these 
with real time connectivity have been operationalised so far. The specifications 
of BPR and data buoys have been finalized. 
(d) and (e) the experts have suggested creation of bio-shield with 
appropriate vegetation including mangroves along the coast to minimise 
the impacts of tsunami. Under the mangrove Management Action Plan of 
the Ministry of Environment and Forests, 35 mangrove areas in the country 
have been identified for intensive conservation and management. 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
Tokyo-led Asian broad band programme 
*265. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that India and Japan have signed an MoU for 
participation of India in the Tokyo-led Asian Broad Band Programme; and 
(b) if so, the details of the agreement? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN): (a) and (b) No, Sir. 
However, on 18th January, 2005, a Joint Statement was signed by the Minister 
of Communications and Information Technology of India and the Minister for 
Internal Affairs & Communications of Japan in Tokyo, Japan during the visit of 
Hon'ble Minister of Communications and Information Technology to Japan. 
In the Joint Statement, the two Mi nisters confirmed that Information 
Communication Technology (ICT) is a major driving force in promoting 
sustainable economic & social development, improving quality of life, helping 
people achieve their full potential and maintaining cultural diversities. 
The two Ministers affirmed that As ia Broad Band Programme, inter-aiia, 
can make a significant contribution to the development of information society in 
both countries as well as in the Asia-Pacific region as a whole. The two Ministers 
further confirmed the necessity to strengthen cooperation between Japan and India in 
the field of ICT including encouraging the use of affordable technologies for 
broadband network.

War against terrorism by Pakistan 
*269. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that JKLF leader Yasin Malik confessed before the 
media during his visit to Islamabad in June, 2005 that Pakistan Information 
Minister is the person in-charge of  terrorist training camps across our 
international border; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the ground reality, revealed by the confession, has been 
contrary to the assurances given by the Pakistan President in January, 2004; 
(d) whether Government confronted Pakistani administration with it, 
besides the international community engaged in war against terrorism; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof, including response of the respective 
Governments in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) to (e) Media reports indicate that JKLF leader 
Yasin Malik had told the media, at a meeting during an exhibition in 
Islamaoad on June 13, 2005, that Pakistan information Minister Sheikh Rashid 
Ahmed had set up a camp for training militants in PaKistan. 
Government has stated that this revelation was a matter or great concern. It was 
particularly serious tnat people directly involved in such activities continued to 
occupy high positions in Pakistan. Government's stand remains tnat no 
effective action has been taken by Pakistan to dismantle the infrastructure of 
support to terrorism on a permanent oasis. Government has, in its interaction with 
Pakistan at ail levels, continuously stressed the fact that Pakistan has so far not 
taken any significant action to dismantle the infrastructure of support to 
terrorism, such as communications, launching pads, training camps, funding, 
etc. Government has made it clear to Pakistan that the premise on which the 
present dialogue process is based is the commitment of January 6,2004 by 
Pakistan not to permit any territory under Pakistan's control to be used to 
support terrorism in any manner. 
13 

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
Pakistan has denied that Sheikh Rashid had been running terrorist training 
camps. 
Recruitment of drivers by KGL 
*270. SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Will the Minister of OVERSEAS AND 
INDIAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the renewed 
activities of Kuwait and Gulf Link Transport Company of Kuwait to recruit 
drivers and other categories of workers for Iraq; and 
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government to safeguard Indian citizens from 
being lured into hazardous employment in Iraq? 
THE PRIME MINISTER (DR. MANMOHAN SINGH): (a) and (b): 
1. There have been Press reports about M/s. Kuwait and Gulf Link 
Transport Co., Kuwait (KGL) recruiting truck and trailer drivers for 
Iraq. 
2. KGL had been placed in the Prior Approval Category (PAC) in 2001. It 
was removed from the PAC list in Nov. 2004 on the recommendation 
of the Embassy of India, Kuwait. 
3. In the wake of recent Press reports  about the activities of KGL, all 
Protectors of Emigrants have been directed not to grant emigration 
clearance at their level w.e.f. 22.07.2005 to Indian workers proposed to be 
deployed by KGL but refer the proposals to the Protector General of 
Emigrants. 
4. Further, the practice of a speci fic endorsement "NOT VALID FOR 
TRAVEL TO IRAQ" on the passports of workers going to Kuwait and 
Jordan, has been extended to all workers going to all Gulf countries. 
Country among maritime nations 
*271. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether despite the long coastline, India is not rated among the top 20 
maritime nations; and 
14 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the measures that Government would adopt to improve the 
situation? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI TR. BAALU). (a) No, Sir. As per Lloyd's Register Fairplay 'World Fleet 
Statistics 2004', India stands at 19th rank among the maritime nations in so far as 
nation's gross tonnage is concerned. The gross tonnage of Indian fleet was 8.11 
million GT as on 1.8.2005. The position is still better in terms of DWT, where 
India's rank is 13th in the world. In terms of supply of seafarers, India has major 
strength and it ranks 6th in the world. 
(b) In order to further improve India's rank as a maritime nation, 
Government of India has taken the following important measures: 
Augmentation of Tonnage 
• The Government has announced introduction of tonnage tax from the 
financial year 2004-05 for the Shipping Industry. 
• Dredgers have also been included in the tonnage tax regime from 2005-
06. 
• The Government of India is in the process of finalizing a 
comprehensive policy for the Maritime Sector. 
• Service tax relaxation has been granted for shipping sector for some of the 
services taken by them abroad. 
• 100% FDI is allowed in shipping sector. 
Promotion of Seafaring: 
• Private investment in Maritime training institutions has been allowed, 
resulting in increase in number of trained Indian Seafarers who can be 
employed on world fleet. 
Power target through existing reactor 
*272.   SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that by 2020, India plans to be a nuclear reactor global 
leader; 
15 

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
(b) if so, the details of the action plan to achieve the target; 
(c) the amount of power produced by the existing reactors; and 
(d) the power target by 2020 through these reactors? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) W ith 14 reactors (2770 MWe) in 
operation and 9 reactors (4460  MWe) under construction, an excellent safety 
record of 239 reactor years, project gestation period of 5 years and a 
comprehensive capability in the front end and back end of the fuel cycle, India is 
already one of the few countries having a significant nuclear power programme. 
As regards small and medium  size reactors, India has an edge since in having 
small reactors in operation in large numbers. Further capacity addition will 
reinforce the country's position in this regard. 
(b) The present installed nuclear power capacity of 2770 MWe is expected to 
reach 7280 MWe by March 2011 with the progressive completion of projects 
under construction. More projects are also planned so as to reach the projected 
nuclear power capacity of 20000 MWe by the year 2020. 
(c) During the year 2004-05 the total electricity generation from nuclear power 
reactors in the country was 17010 Million Units (MUs). 
(d) The generation target for the X Plan is 82495 MUs. of which 60160 MUs 
has already been achieved by July 2005. No generation targets have been fixed for 
the period beyond the X Plan.

1885. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: W ill the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether India's inability to expand its present nuclear power generation 
capacity, which cover only 3 per cent of our total requirements is due to 
inadequate supplies of uranium and technological assistance coupled with embargo 
by a cartel called Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG); 
(b) whether the NSG operates a blanket ban on technology and materials trade 
with black-listed countries, including India; and 
(c) If so, whether US has offered civilian nuclear energy cooperation with India 
which could lead the NSG to reconsider the ban currently in force? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) and (b) No, Sir. India has formulated a 
comprehensive indigenous three-stage nuclear power programme to expand its 
nuclear power generating capacity to 20,000 MW by the year 2020. 
International cooperation can supplement our indigenous efforts. However at 
present the Nuclear Suppliers' Group (NSG) guidelines prevent trade in nuclear 
technology and materials with India. According to these guidelines such items can 
be supplied to a non-nuclear-weapon State only when that State has brought into 
force an agreement with the IAEA requiring the application of safeguards on 
all its current and future peaceful activities. 
(c) The Joint Statement issued during the recent visit of Prime Minister to the 
US, states inter-alia "the United States will work with friends and allies to 
adjust international regimes to enable full civil nuclear energy cooperation and 
trade with India, including but not limited to expeditious consideration of fuel 
supplies for safeguarded nuclear reactors at Tarapur. In the meantime, the United 
States will encourage its partners to also consider this request epeditiously". 
Accident in CCL mine in Hazaribagh 
1886. SHRI LALIT SURI: 
SHRI DARA SINGH CHAUHAN: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether a number of workers got trapped inside the Central Coal Fields 
Ltd. (CCL) Saunda mine in Hazaribagh on the 14th June, 2005; 
32 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) the number, out of them, who lost their lives and those who could be 
rescued; 
(c) whether the cause of the accident has been investigated; if so, the findings 
thereof and the action taken thereon; 
(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken to prevent such mishaps; and 
(e) the nature of assistance givea to the families of those who lost their lives 
in the mishap? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYAN RAO): (a) and (b) As per information received from Coal India 
Limited (CIL), at the end of the third shift of 14.6.2005, i.e. the morning of 
15.6.2005, fourteen employees (12 workmen and 25tipervisors) did not come 
out of Old Bansgara Incline of Central Saunda Colliery of Central Coalfields 
Ltd. (CCL), in Hazaribagh district, Jharkhand. The rescue and recovery 
operations along with action to de water the drawned area were taken 
immediately. Services of Naval divers for rescue of survivors were also utilized, 
but the precious lives of all the above 14 persons, who were trapped inside the 
mine, could not be saved. 
(c) The Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS) under the Ministry of 
Labour, which is the statutory body for enforcement of safety statutes in mines in 
the country, is conducting enquiry, under the Mines Act, 1952, into the 
accident. The enquiry is stated to be in progress. 
Besides, Ministry of Coal had constituted a committee under chairmanship 
of Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Central Mine Planning and Degine 
Institute Limited for holding a Departmental enquiry. The Committee has 
since submitted its report, which is under consideration. The main findings of 
the report are as under. 
(i) The accident was caused by fall of a large area of standing roof in the 
decoaled area leading to air blast. The presence of weak zone of strata 
might have contributed to the fall of roof which also resulted in inrush of 
water through the caved area from the water logged old workings of 
overlying seam. Ineffective dewatering of the overlying seam before and 
during depillaring is the major cause for this inundation. 
33 

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
(ii) Acts of negligence and dereliction of duty have taken place on the part 
of CCL officials. 
(d) To prevent such mishaps and to improve the status of safety in 
mines, following steps are being taken by the coal companies:— 
• Thurst on training and retaining of workmen, supervisors and 
managers to increase safety awareness. 
• Issue of guidelines for safer opera tions in identified thrust areas 
through circulars. 
• Promoting participation of workers in safety management. 
• Promoting self-regulation by management. 
• Tri-partite and Bi-partite review of safety status at various levels. 
• Observance of safety week and safety campaigns. 
• Generating safety awareness and information dissemination. 
• National Conference on Safety in Mines. 
• National Safety Awards. 
• Interactions at different forums with a view to promote safety, health and 
welfare of persons employed in mines. 
• Introduction to the concept of Risk Assessment, preparation of Safety 
Management Plan and Development of Emergency Response System. 
• Facilitating introduction of new technology in mining with low 
potential risk. 
(e) As reported by CIL, apart from compensation payable under the 
Workmen's Compensation Act, ex-gratia, life-cover, gratuity, leave 
encashment, benevolent fund, employment to one dependant of the 
deceased have been given. The amount of compensation paid to the affected 
families varies from Rs. 5.32 lakhs  to Rs. 6.86 lakhs depending upon the 
age and length of service of the d eceased persons. In addition to the 
above, kin of each deceased will be paid by Insurance Company against 
group insurance accident scheme which will be about Rs. 5 lakhs. Provident 
34 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Fund through Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPF), in the region 
of Rs. 3 to 4 lakhs will be paid to the dependents and pension to wife and two 
dependent sons will also be disbursed by CMPF. 
Besides, the Hon'ble Prime Minister has sanctioned an ex-gratia of Rs. 
1,00,000/- from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund to the next of each of 
kin of the deceased. CIL has also been advised to make payment of Rs. 1 lakh to

1890. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether there is an acute shortage of coal supply in the country, more 
so in Orissa, 
(b) if so, whether as a result of this industrial production of iron, steel and 
other metals have been affected severely; and 
(c) what are the reasons for this shortage despite a vast reserve of coal of 250 
billion tonnes and lignite of 36 billion tonnes in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYAN RAO): (a) There is a gap between demand and indigenous 
supply of coal. This gap also affects the State of Orissa on pro-rata basis. Coal 
companies have taken adequate steps to enhance production from 323 million 
tonnes of coal during 2004-05 to 343 million tonnes projected for the year 2005-
06. Despite this there is likely to be a gap of about 39 million tonnes of 
indigenous coal in the country. This gap is proposed to be met through imports 
of about 31 million tonnes and by making efforts to increase domestic 
production.

industries meet their requirement, Government has also reduced import duty to 
5% for all grades of coal except coki ng coal with ash less than 12% on which 
import duty has been abolished. 
(c) Production of coal is based on Annual Action Plan targets set by the 
Planning Commission and over the years coal companies have achieved 6% 
production growth. Coal production has a  long gestation period. When coal 
production is planned based on estimated demand by the Planning Commission 
and the actual demand exceeds the estimation, the mismatch occurs.

Parity in procurement of equipment 
1913. SHRI V. NA RAYANASAMY : Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that BSNL is demanding for parity in procurement of 
equipment with private telecom operators; and 
(b) if so, Government's reaction in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Given 
the nature of public and private sectors, there cannot be an absolute parity between 
them in the matter of procurement. While BSNL has not demanded any parity in 
procurement of equipment with private telecom operators, its concern was in 
respect of the proposed initiative of promoting indigenous telecom 
manufacturing in its procurements. 
(b) Indigenous manufacture of telephone equipments is felt desirable with 
the objective, inter alia, of the availability of desired quality/standard products at 
competitive rates, immediate availability of after-sales services and development 
of new technologies in the Country. A procurement framework, whereby only 
vendors who indigenously manufacture (or have definite plans to do so) certain 
telecom products are alone eligible" for procurement is under active 
consideration by BSNL and MTNL.

†1915. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that quality of mobile 
telephone services in several parts of th e Uttaranchal has deteriorated steeply 
during the last few months;

hampered; and 
(c) if so, the details of the steps being taken for improving the quality of 
mobile phone services in Uttaranchal? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) and 
(b) In terms of Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Act 1997, 
TRAI is, inter-alia, mandated to monitor the Quality of Service (QoS) 
parameters of the mobile services provided by licensed mobile service 
providers in the country. As per the performance monitoring reports 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
71

submitted by the mobile service providers of Uttar Pradesh (West) service area, no 
major deterioration in the quality of service of mobile operators is notified by TRAI.

has been observed in Uttaranchal due to limitation in its capacity. Also, the 
mobile service" has been affected on some occasions especially in Rishikesh-
Badrinath Highway on failure of Opti cal Fibre Cable (OFC) media due to 
widening of the roads.

restoring the media breakdown promptly. Also BSNL is expanding the mobile 
network capacity in Uttaranchal by about 2 lakhs lines progressively during the

1968. DR. VI JAY MALLYA: Will the Minister of OCEAN DEVELOPMENT

setting up a long-term and round-the clock National Tsunami warning system;

centres? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) to (c) It is proposed to set up a 
Tsunami and Storm Surge Early Warning system by the Department of Ocean 
Development with its Centre at the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information 
Services (INCOIS), Hyderabad. The system will comprise of the following 
components:

real time occurrence of tsunamigenic earthquakes.

• Tide gauge and data buoys networking. 
• Modelling of the inundation scenarios for the entire coast. 
• Collection of information, analysis and generating status advisories. 
The Centre is proposed to operate on round the clock basis.

Meeting of NDC 
†1981. SHRI R.S. GAVAI: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a meeting of National Development Council was 
held on 27th and 28th June in Vigyan Bhavan; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
126 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the issue discussed in the meeting; 
(c) the recommendation made to be implemented in future; and 
(d) the steps Government would take to implement these 
recommendations? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI 
M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a)to (c) The National Development Council met 
under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister on 27th and 28th June, 2005 to 
consider the Mid-Term Appraisal of the Tenth Five Year Plan and took the 
following decisons: 
1. The NDC expressed broad agreemen t with the goals and policies 
suggested in the Mid-Term Appraisal which could act as a blue print 
for further action on development matters in the Tenth Plan and as the 
starting paint for initiating work on the Eleventh Five Year Plan. The 
Planning Commission was directed to examine a number of valuable 
suggestions made by Chief Ministers during the course of discussions 
which require a review of some of the policies, programmes and 
approaches. 
2. The NDC took note of the concern expressed by the Chief Ministers about 
issues relating to State finances, particularly the effects of the 
recommendations of the 12th Finance Commission, the level of 
permissible market borrowings and interest costs on borrowings as also 
issues relating to mineral royalties and externally aided projects. It was 
decided to set up a Committee separately under the Finance Minister 
to examine relevant issues relating to the debt burden of States and 
debt relief with reference to their debt outstandings against the Natioal 
Small Saving Fund (NSSF). 
3. Recognizing the fact that agriculture and irrigation have been a 
common theme in the interventions of the Chief Ministers, and that 
rejuvenating the agricultural credit system, providing some measure of 
relief to farmers, improving the quality of our extension work, 
attending to the specific needs and problems of dry lands and 
wastelands and enhancing investments in irrigation have emerged as 
common concerns, the NDC agreed  to form a Sub-Committee for 
drawing up implementable action plans in agriculture and related issues. 
The NDC Sub-Committee is expected to submit its report 
127 

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
within the next six months for inclusion in the Approach Paper to the 
Eleventh Five Year Plan. 
4. On the Employment Gurantee Act, the suggestions that payment of 
wages should be mostly in cash since there were problems in movement 
of food grains to backward areas and that being the self-targeting 
programme, the Employment Guarantee should cover non-BPL families 
were noted by the NDC, and it was directed to consider them for inclusion 
in the final draft of the National Employment Guarantee Bill. 
5. To look into the need for providing adequate flexibility in the design of 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes, such as Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, the 
National Rural Health Mission and Bharat Nirman etc., to take account 
of state level realities and priorities, as well as the feasibility of their transfer 
to States/UTs or amalgamation into four or five broad heads with the 
freedom to develop locally relevant programmes, the NDC directed the 
Planning Commission to consider setting up an Expert Group to develop 
concrete proposals for restructuring the CSS, in consultation with the 
concerned Ministries/Departments. 
6. Recognizing that improvement in physical infrastructure has also 
emerged as a common priority and in creased private participation has 
now become a necessity to mobilize the resources needed to achieve its 
expansion and upgradation, the NDC observed that successful 
promotion of private participation in infrastructure requires a well-designed 
framework of policies in which investors have the assurance that 
standards of services will be maintained and concessions w ill be 
transparently awarded and directed the Central Government to work towards 
evolving such a framework, which could be adopted by the States. 
7. The Planning Commission was directed to begin work on the 
Approach to the Eleventh Five Year Plan with a view to submit it for 
National Development Council's approval by the end of December, 2005. 
(d) Steps have already been initiated on the decisions/directions 
concerning Planning Commission. Besides, Planning Commission has also 
circulated the decisions/directions of the National Development Council

BPL status to a person 
1985. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the parameters/criteria for granting status of Below Poverty Line to a person; 
(b) whether they are different for urban and rural areas; 
(c) the total number of Below Poverty Line persons in the country with State-
wise break up; 
(d) what percentage it is of total population of the country as well as States; 
(e) whether there is any improvement or deterioration in Below Poverty Line 
scenario in the country; and 
138 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(f) if so, its details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI M.V RAJASEKHARAN): (a) and (b) The Planning Commission has 
adopted per capita consumption expenditure needed to attain a minimum amount 
of calorie intake out of food consumption along with a minimum am ount of 
non-food expenditure in order to meet the requirements of clothing, shelter, 
transport etc. as the criterion to determine the persons living below the poverty 
line. The per capita consumption norm has been fixed at Rs. 49.09 per month in 
rural areas and Rs. 56.64 per month in urban areas at 1973-74 prices at national 
level corresponding to a basket of goods and services anchored on a norm of 
per capita daily calorie requirement of 2400 kcal in rural areas and 2100 kcal in 
urban areas. As per the Expert Group on 'Estimation of Proportion and Number 
of Poor' (Lakadawala Committee), the state-specific poverty lines are derived from 
the basket of goods and services consumed by the national poverty line class, 
using state-specific price indices and inter-state price differentials. The prescribed 
per capita consumption expenditure for determination of people living below 
poverty line for different states are regularly updated using state-specific cost of 
living indices, that is, Consumer Price Indices for Agricultural Labourers (CPIAL) 
for rural areas and Consumer Price Indices for Industrial Workers (CPIIW) for

Research in Biotechnology 
1988. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: W ill the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Department of Biotechnology has selected new 
areas for research in the field of Biotechnology; 
142 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) what exactly is bio-separation; 
(c) whether any research is going on in the country on bio-separation; and 
(d) if so, in what way it helps the common man? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) Bio-separation is the process for purification of targeted bio-molecule by 
applying various techniques. Bio-molecules are usually present in very low 
concentrations. Further, the impurities could have physicochemical properties 
similar to those of the target compound of interest. Several separation steps 
are needed to obtain the target molecule  sufficiently pure to make it suitable 
for a specific use. The primary downstream operation is the removal of 
insolubles (e.g. by sedimentation, filtration, centrifugation, permeation by 
membranes), followed by isolation of the compound (e.g. by precipitation, 
extraction, adsorption, separation by membranes) and final purification (e.g. by 
crystallization, chromatography). 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) Bio-separation is useful for various biotechnological applications 
involving large scale purification and protein separation. It is one of the steps 
involved in the process for preparation of therapeutically important compounds, 
antibiotics, food supplements and enzymatic preparations. It also has application in 
water and air purification systems leading to reduction in environmental pollution. 
Gene Silencing 
1989. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Hyderabad based Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CO 
M.B.) led by Manika Pal Bhadra and Utpal Bhadra under C.C.M.B., Director 
Shri Lalji Singh has unraveled the Mystery behind Gene Silencing paving the way 
for detecting the mechanisms that prevents cancer in human beings; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
143 

RAJYA SABHA [11 August, 2005] 
(c) details of action taken so far in the direction of developing these new 
findings towards Pharmaceutical therapy for Patenting and marketing the product 
to save several millions of cancer victims in the world from death, every year; 
(d) whether Government would assure of releasing special package of funds 
in this most important and crucial field of "Gene Silencing" for speedy results; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) Dr. Manika Pal Bhadra and Utpal Bhadra first demonstrated that gene 
silencing is involved in heterochroma tin which is required for rapid cell 
division; these results have already been published in the prestigious journal 
Science (2004). In continua tion to their work they recently found that several 
micro RNAs are involved in heterochromatin formation. Diseases coupled with cell 
division and cell proliferation, such as various types of Cancers, appear to be 
controlled by heterochromatin formation and its functioning. Understanding the 
role of gene silencing through micro RNAs thus might pave a way to use it as a 
possible therapy for cancers and other related diseases, which involve cell 
cycle controls. 
(c) and (d) Several measures are being taken in the direction of the 
development of therapy for cancer. Besides preparing a detailed progress report for 
the application of these results for can cer treatment Scientists at CCMB have 
also prepared a detailed document for patent application. The programme as part 
of R&D activity of CCMB is receiving necessary financial support. 
(e) Question does not arise.

glasses shall not be used in cars;

Uniform system for driving licences 
2019. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government or the NHAI have received any proposal for a 
uniform system of giving driving licences from the Road Safety Forum in 
Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) the proposals under consideration for arranging modern and efficient driving 
licence examinations and efficient system of giving licences, nation-wise; 
(c) whether poor and varied systems of giving licences for drivers in the country 
has created a pool of unsafe and dangerous drivers along highway; 
(d) the steps proposed to consider the system of having a national system 
of giving driving licences; and 
(e) the reasons for not taking up this proposal? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI K.H. MUNIAPPA): (a) and (b) 
Chapter-ll of the Motor Vehicles Act,  1988 and Chaper-ll of the Central 
Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 prescribe a body of rules for testing and 
examination prior to grant of driving licences. These rules also prescribe the 
procedure for granting the licences and the validity in terms of various classes of 
vehicles and the time period. Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 also provides 
for issuance of smart-card based driving licences, based on a standardised 
software, developed and made available by Central Government to the States. 
The States have been empowered to prescribe the date from which such smart-card 
based driving licences shall be issued in the States. 
(c) Compliance with the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and 
Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and the procedure laid down therein rules 
out licensing of unsafe and dangerous drivers. 
(d) and (e) Section 28 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 empowers the State 
Governments for appointment of the licensing authorities and determining 
their jurisdiction, functions etc. There is no proposal to have a national system of 
giving driving licences as the same is the responsibility 
184 

[11 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
of the State Governments in terms of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central 
Government has no machinery to implement the provisions of Motor 
Vehicles Act, 1988 by itself.
